column2: Verify that user can perform 2 Intake to Payments full flow for 1 CXO
column4: one CXO of 100 qty funds two 50-qty intakes, each paid in full
column5:
1. Create ONE CXO (line item qty 100 x 2,000 = 200,000) and approve it to Released.
2. Write a private fixture copy per chain, both seeded with that savedCxo and with invoice-number seeds 500 apart. Every save*Code helper rewrites pages/NSEFoundationData.json, so two chains sharing it would open each other's PO/invoice.
3. Reserve the run's whole invoice-number range in the shared fixture UP FRONT — a run that dies mid-flight has still burned its numbers on the server, and the app blocks a duplicate reference by DISABLING Proceed (silent block).
4. CHAIN A - intake (qty 50, linked to the CXO) -> approve to Released -> Process -> Send For Sourcing -> RFX -> approve -> quote (Commercial, INR, unit rate 2,000) -> foreclose -> award -> PR edit+submit -> wait Processed/Completed -> PRC -> PO -> approve -> GRN (received = PO qty) -> approve to Inwarded.
5. CHAIN A invoice: PO -> Create -> Invoice -> upload document, invoice no. + date, period/extra billing No -> FIX -> Item Matching -> tick the chain's GRN -> Submit -> approve every stage until the invoice settles.
6. CHAIN A payment: POST the acknowledgement (EXPENSE_RECORD_NO = invoice code, response_body_reference = invoice number) -> assert Accounted -> + Payment with paid amount = invoice amount, a unique UTR and today's date -> Submit -> Transactions tab shows the payment Completed.
7. CHAIN B - repeat steps 4-6 with a SECOND intake (qty 50) on the SAME CXO, which by now has 100,000 consumed and 100,000 remaining.
8. Assert the two chains are genuinely separate: different intake codes, different invoice codes, different invoice references, different UTRs.
9. Carry the invoice counter forward into the shared fixture, then restore the other fixtures.
NOTE the chains run SEQUENTIALLY (RUN_PARALLEL=false). Parallel is wired up and was tried: the app loses one of two surrogate quotes submitted at the same moment as the same supplier (RFX-26-268 stayed Released at "0 out of 1 Supplier" while RFX-26-267 quoted fine).
RESUME POINTS, so a late failure costs only its own segment: S1_CXO_CODE/S1_CXO_ID (reuse a CXO), S1_RESUME_PR_ID (from a Completed PR), S1_RESUME_INVOICE_ID/CODE/NUMBER (from a settled invoice). S1_ONLY=A|B runs one chain.
column6: One CXO funds two complete Intake-to-Payment flows; both invoices reach Accounted and both payments show Completed, on two distinct sets of records.
column7:
PASS (48.2 min, 2026-09-10). CXO-FNSE-26-436 (200,000) carried both flows: chain A INT-FNSE-26-448 -> PO-NSEFN-26-254 -> Invoice-FNSE-26-410 paid 100,000 (UTR ...822651); chain B INT-FNSE-26-449 -> PO-NSEFN-26-255 -> Invoice-FNSE-26-412 paid 100,000 (UTR ...846307). All four distinctness assertions held.
Nine defects were fixed to get here. Pre-existing, in shared helpers: (a) approveSourcingUntilReleased inferred "approved" from a MISSING Pending Approval badge and returned with the RFX still pending; (b) _waitForApproveButton allowed only 4s per attempt and reported "Approve not visible" on pages that did offer it (12s now); (c) completeIntakeSubmissionPopup clicked Proceed while the Process Request dialog was still loading it disabled; (d) waitForPrStatus waited on the TRANSIENT "Processed" and burned 54 polls while PR-NSEFN-26-167 sat Completed (accepts an array now); (e) readInvoiceAmount read the page's "0.00" placeholder and entered a ZERO payment (polls for non-zero now); (f) the ack POST had no retry and lost a whole chain to one ETIMEDOUT.
Also fixed in this spec: the invoice counter was only carried forward on success, so failed runs burned references the next run then collided with.

column2: Verify revert pending budget can be done for the partially processed CXO
column4: half the CXO is consumed by a submitted PR; the other half is revertable
column5:
1. Create a CXO worth 200,000 (qty 100 x 2,000) and approve it to Released.
2. Create an intake for HALF of it (qty 50 = 100,000), approve to Released.
3. Process -> Send For Sourcing -> RFX -> approve -> quote -> foreclose.
4. Award, then PR edit + submit. THE PR SUBMIT IS THE STEP THAT CONSUMES BUDGET - see the note below.
5. Open the CXO VIEW PAGE (per QA) -> More -> Revert Pending Budget, and READ the row without submitting: Transaction Value / Consumed Value / Pending Value / the pre-filled Rollback Value.
6. Assert the split exactly: transaction 200,000, consumed 100,000, pending 100,000, rollback pre-filled 100,000.
7. Submit the revert with remarks, and assert the amount submitted equals the pending 100,000.
8. Re-open the dialog and assert "No pending budget to revert".
WHY THE CHAIN RUNS PAST THE INTAKE: budget is consumed when the PR is SUBMITTED - not at intake release, and NOT at the award. Measured on CXO-FNSE-26-406, whose award (AWD-FNSE-26-170, 100,000) left requisition 1134 in Pending Review as PR-DRAFT: before the PR was submitted the dialog read consumed 0 / pending 200,000; after, consumed 100,000 / pending 100,000. The first run of this test stopped at the award and read consumed 0. Corroborating: CXO-FNSE-26-390 (two intakes merely Released) and CXO-FNSE-26-391 (intake Processed, RFX only Quoted) both read consumed 0 / pending 200,000.
column6: A CXO with half its value consumed by a submitted PR offers the other half in Revert Pending Budget; reverting it leaves nothing pending and does not disturb the consumed half.
column7: PASS (6.9 min, 2026-09-09; re-verified on current code). CXO-FNSE-26-414 (200,000) -> INT-FNSE-26-415 (qty 50) -> PR-NSEFN-26-154 submitted. Dialog read transaction=200000 consumed=100000 pending=100000 rollback=100000; the revert submitted 100,000 with remarks, and re-opening reported "No pending budget to revert".

column2: Verify that an RFX Award created from a CXO Intake can be cancelled and a new Award can be created successfully.
column4: a rejected award can be cancelled and the RFX awarded again to a fresh PR
column5:
1. Build the chain: CXO -> Intake -> convert to RFX (2 approvals to Released) -> supplier quote at Rs 2,000 -> foreclose.
2. Analysis tab -> Award -> allocate the full pending qty (100) -> submit into the award workflow. The first award is deliberately NOT approved - rejecting it mid-workflow IS the scenario.
3. Reject the award during approvals. The award workflow often assigns its first stage to another user, so rejectAward reassigns to NSEF Support Admin and retries before giving up.
4. Stay on the award page (do not navigate away first) and go More -> Cancel. The "Cancel Award" dialog is award-specific: confirm is "Cancel Award", the DISMISS is "Keep Award", and the reason textarea is mandatory.
5. The app redirects to the RFX Awards view by itself - the ONLY place the AWARD's own status is shown (the award detail page renders the parent RFX badge and the line item status, both of which read "Awarded" on a rejected award). Assert Status = Cancelled and Requisition = "-".
6. Analysis tab -> Award again -> allocate the released qty -> submit -> approve through to Completed.
7. Assert the re-award produced a requisition. A test that only asserted "status = Cancelled" would miss the real failure mode: qty staying locked so no further award is possible.
column6: A rejected award can be cancelled; the cancellation releases its allocated quantity back to the pending pool, and the RFX can be awarded again through to a requisition.
column7: PASS (8.2 min, 2026-09-11, single end-to-end run). CXO-FNSE-26-440 -> INT-FNSE-26-453 -> RFX-26-299. Award #1 AWD-FNSE-26-203 (/rfx/1536/awards/757) rejected then cancelled - the Awards view read Status "Cancelled", Requisition "-", Total Value Rs 200,000. The re-award then found Pending Awarded Quantity back at "100.00", which is the proof the cancellation RELEASED the qty; award #2 approved to Completed (round 2, after reassigning the stage to NSEF Support Admin) and produced requisition PR-DRAFT. Verified earlier on the same code on RFX-26-298 / AWD-FNSE-26-201 (re-award half, 1.5 min). TWO TEST BUGS were fixed to get here, both in the harness - the app was correct at every step: (a) clickAwardBackArrow waited 15s for a back arrow the app legitimately removes, because cancelling an award self-redirects to /quote-requests/<id>/awards; (b) awardsTabValueFor used normalize-space(text()), which evaluates only the FIRST text node - React emits "{label}:" as two text nodes ("Award Code" + ":"), so it matched ZERO nodes for EVERY label on the Awards view and readAwardSummary silently returned empty strings, surfacing as the misleading "expects an already-cancelled award / received ''". NOTE the requisition assertion is /PR/i, which also accepts the PR-DRAFT placeholder (the app's literal for an unsubmitted draft requisition, cf. scenario 2) - worth tightening to require PR-DRAFT or a real PR-NSEFN code.

column2: Verify that Intake can be created using Bulk Upload
column4: 100 line items uploaded from the downloaded template reach a Released intake
column5:
1. Intake create page -> select template -> expand sections -> fill EVERY header field via fillIntakeHeaderFields, with NO manual line row, so the uploaded rows are the whole grid (exactly 100, not 101).
2. Bulk Upload (top right) -> Download Template. Saved under downloads/ and asserted non-empty. The download-vs-new-tab race is kept: this app opens a tab instead often enough that a bare waitForEvent('download') hangs and reports a working feature as broken.
3. Write the SAME line item 100 times into the workbook the app just served (exceljs): Item Name "Manpower (T&M)", Qty 100, UOM NOS, Delivery/Billing "Mumbai - Exchange Plaza BKC", Unit Price 2000.
4. Upload it through the FILE CHOOSER, then wait for the streaming /api/capp/v4/intakes/excel-upload response and require its "complete" frame - a 200 alone is not success.
5. Assert the grid holds 100 line items by scrolling the virtualised grid and collecting its serial column (highest = 100 AND distinct = 100).
6. Potential suppliers -> Submit -> Process Request popup -> approve every stage until Released.
column6: An intake whose 100 line items come entirely from a Bulk Upload of the downloaded template submits and approves through to Released.
column7: PASS (1.5 min, 2026-09-11, first run). Template served as Intake_Create_20260911.xlsx (27,305 bytes); 100 rows written (29,090 bytes); excel-upload completed; grid serials read highest 100 / distinct 100; INT-FNSE-26-454 submitted and Released after 6 workflow steps (stage 2 offered no action button, so the helper reassigned to NSEF Support Admin - normal for this env). THREE TRAPS found live and encoded in the helpers, not the spec: (a) the Bulk Upload dialog's own input[type=file] is INERT - setInputFiles on it produces no request, no toast and no grid change; the "Upload File" button mounts a real OS chooser, so the upload must go through waitForEvent('filechooser'); (b) template columns H (Remarks) and L (Key/itemKey) carry a custom dataValidation whose formula is literally FALSE, i.e. they reject every value - H looks like ordinary free text and is a trap; (c) the line-item grid is VIRTUALISED (~31 of 100 rows mounted at a time), so a DOM row count asserts 31 and fails a working feature - the serial column must be harvested while scrolling. The template is downloaded FRESH each run rather than committed as a fixture, so a column or validation change breaks this test by design. exceljs 4.4.0 was verified to round-trip the protected template losslessly (sheetProtection SHA-512 hash intact, all 6 dataValidations with identical sqrefs, header row byte-identical, 1002 rows preserved). The app accepted 100 IDENTICAL rows - no duplicate-item rejection at upload.

This scenario must NOT reuse a stored CXO: budget is consumed at PR SUBMIT, so a reused CXO drains and submitPr then stalls on a Workflow dialog whose Submit is disabled behind "Budget Amount is exceeded" plus a mandatory empty "Budget Amend Request".
2. Reject the PO during approvals (rejectCappDoc(..., 'PO')).
3. Edit it -> lower the line quantity 100 -> 50 -> submit, confirming the follow-up workflow dialog.
4. Open the PRC's Requisition Conversion View from the PR's Transactions -> Conversions.
5. EXPAND the RC (Rate Contract) section - the Convert to PO button does not exist in the DOM until it is expanded.
6. Assert Convert to PO is enabled and BLUE (computed background rgb(51, 136, 235)).
7. Click it -> /requisition-conversion/<id>/newPo -> set the two mandatory fields (Inward Required = Yes, Inward Matching Criterion = Quantity) -> Submit -> confirm the workflow dialog.
8. Assert the conversion lands on /purchase-orders/<id> with a PO code.
column6: The quantity freed by lowering the PO during a reject-edit returns to the PRC and can be converted into a second PO.
column7: PASS (17.2 min, 2026-09-11, certification run). PR-NSEFN-26-173 -> PRC-NSEFN-26-168; the PO was rejected, its qty lowered 100 -> 50, and the PR moved to "Partially Converted". The RC section, once expanded, offered Convert to PO enabled with background rgb(51, 136, 235) (the app's primary blue); conversion 509 produced PO-NSEFN-26-260 at /purchase-orders/1095 with "Purchase Order Submitted successfully". Corroborated earlier the same day on PRC conversion 507 -> PO-NSEFN-26-258. THREE TRAPS, all encoded in the helpers: (a) the Convert to PO button is INSIDE the collapsed RC (Rate Contract) section and is absent from the DOM until expanded - the first run dumped the collapsed view, saw only More/Overview/Process/Transactions and reported "Convert to PO: null"; (b) buildToPoViaCapp ends by opening the PO in a NEW TAB and the actions object switches to it (this.page = newPage), so a spec that keeps using the `page` fixture silently drives the stale PR tab - 10 call sites had to move to a.page; (c) the edit pencil is not always present immediately after the reject re-renders the header, so editPoLowerQtyAndSubmit reloads and retries twice before giving up. The "Converting to PO" form has exactly two mandatory fields and is otherwise pre-filled from the PRC.

column2: Verify that an Invoice is moved to Disputed status when there is a quantity mismatch between the GRN and Invoice for a quantity-based PO.
column4: an invoice for more than the GRN received quantity is Disputed
column5:
1. Build the full chain CXO -> ... -> PO, then create a GRN with Received set to 50 against a PO quantity of 100.
   (setGrnReceivedQty edits the AG-grid cell; the clear uses ControlOrMeta+a, since plain Control+a does not select cell contents on macOS.)
2. Approve the GRN to Inwarded.
3. PO -> Create -> Invoice -> Select PO Items -> Proceed.
4. Upload the document, fill the header, and set the invoice quantity to 100.
5. Submit without matching, and poll the detail page for Disputed.
column6: An invoice for a quantity greater than the GRN received quantity is moved to Disputed.
column7: PASS - verified live 2026-09-08 (3 passed, 30.2 min for 69 + 13). PO-NSEFN-26-227 with GRN INW-NSEFN-26-116 received 50 against a PO quantity of 100 (log: 'Received set to 50 (cell reads "50")'); the invoice was raised for 100 and Invoice-FNSE-26-382 (/invoices/1154) read Disputed on the FIRST poll. QA's rule, 2026-09-08, verbatim: "if GRN is 50 and invoice is for 100 qty then disputed" / "if GRN is created and during invoice creation if GRN is not matched then disputed" / "if invoice is created without creating a GRN for the PO then Invoice disputed". EACH TEST BUILDS ITS OWN FRESH PO from the full CXO flow (QA confirmed this is required): the three need DIFFERENT GRN states (none / full / partial), and sharing a PO would hit the known "2nd invoice sends the full PO qty" bug, whose SILENT submit block would be indistinguishable from the Disputed-or-not outcome being measured. Invoices are created from CAPP (PO -> Create -> Invoice), the flow that carries the Item Matching step 69 skips. FINDING: Disputed is applied IMMEDIATELY on submit - poll 1 on the detail page - so no approval step is needed, and the Validations popup does NOT refuse an unmatched invoice. TRAP, and it was MY OWN: the afterAll fixture snapshot/restore rolled back invoice.invoiceNumber, which is a MONOTONIC COUNTER, not a fixture. That re-issued a number the server had already consumed and the first run died on the app's duplicate validation (INV-AUTO-119, held by Invoice-FNSE-26-376) with Proceed disabled - the app was entirely correct. Fixed by pages/fixtureGuard.js, which restores fixtures but carries counters FORWARD.

column2: Verify if RFX to Intake is done more than the Intake quantity then error is displayed properly
column4: converting more quantity than the intake holds is refused with an error
column5:
1. REUSE the stored CXO - none is created. This flow never submits the RFX and CXO budget is consumed at PR submit, so the stored CXO is never drawn down (QA, 2026-09-11). Saves ~3 min/run and leaves no junk CXO.
2. Create an Intake the normal way - ONE line item, qty 100 - and approve it to Released.
3. Process -> Send For Sourcing -> expand sections.
4. Start a toast RECORDER (MutationObserver) before touching the quantity.
5. Type 150 into the sourcing Quantity cell via attemptSourcingLineItemQty, which REPORTS rather than asserts - setSourcingLineItemQty asserts the cell took the value, which is right when lowering a qty (scenario 6) and self-defeating where the app is supposed to refuse.
6. The grid accepts it silently, so fill the remaining mandatory fields and Submit, then clear the Workflow Summary dialog's own Submit.

column6: Converting more quantity than the intake holds is refused, and the error names the item and both quantities.
column7: PASS (2.3 min, 2026-09-11). Stored CXO-FNSE-26-435 reused; INT-FNSE-26-461 released at qty 100; asking for 150 is refused on submit with: "Requested quantity exceeds the quantity approved in the intake for: Manpower (T&M) (requested: 150, approved: 100). Please adjust the quantity and try again." THE APP IS CORRECT AND ALWAYS WAS - every earlier failure was in the test. Recorded here because the traps are expensive: (a) the sourcing GRID accepts the over-quantity silently (cell goes 100.00 -> 150.00, no complaint) - the guard is on SUBMIT, not the cell; (b) the error is a TRANSIENT bottom-right toast raised after the Workflow Summary Submit click, so a DOM snapshot taken seconds later sees nothing - five runs reported "no error" and came within one commit of filing a false defect against working functionality. startErrorRecorder() catches toasts via MutationObserver as they are inserted; (c) "is anything on screen" is not an error signal - run 1 matched the destructive-styled "Cancel" BUTTON and run 2 matched the ordinary "Workflow Summary" approval popup, both reporting a guard the app had not shown; (d) the blocked submit fires NO network request and leaves the dialog open, which is the app holding the line, not a broken submit path. Credit: QA spotted the error on screen and pinpointed it to after the Workflow Summary Submit, which is what turned the diagnosis around.

column2: Verify if Intake is converted to RFX from two different tabs in a span of 5 seconds then the later tab should throw error'
column4: the second tab to submit the conversion is rejected
column5:
1. Reuse the stored CXO; create ONE intake (1 line, qty 100) and approve it to Released.
2. Open a SECOND tab in the same browser context, so both tabs share the session exactly as a real user's two tabs would.
3. Take BOTH tabs through Process -> Send For Sourcing -> fill the mandatory fields -> Submit, and PARK each on the open Workflow Summary dialog. submitSourcingEvent() cannot be used here: it clicks Submit and confirms the dialog in one motion, which would commit tab 1 before tab 2 was ever parked. Hence the split into openSourcingWorkflowSummary() and clickWorkflowSummarySubmit().
4. Start a toast recorder in each tab (the messages are transient - see scenario 17).
5. Click Workflow Summary Submit in tab 1, wait 5s, click it in tab 2.
6. Assert the later tab is refused with the real message, that tab 1 actually WON, and that the intake ends with exactly ONE RFX.
column6: The second tab to commit the same conversion is refused with an explanatory error, and only one RFX is created.
column7: PASS (2.5 min, 2026-09-11). Stored CXO-FNSE-26-435; INT-FNSE-26-464 (id 2323). tab1 -> "Sourcing event created successfully" and landed on RFX 1541; tab2 five seconds later -> "One or more line items are already part of an existing RFX" and landed on NO RFX; the intake Transactions tab lists exactly one RFX (RFX-26-302). THE APP IS CORRECT: the guard is at LINE-ITEM level, which is stricter than an intake-level lock and also covers partial conversions, and the message names the actual cause. The conversion is listed on the intake's TRANSACTIONS tab, and the winner's own URL (/quote-requests/<id>/overview) is the direct evidence; (b) run 1 asserted "RFX count <= 1", which ZERO satisfies - so a page that failed to load or a changed code format would have passed silently. It now asserts EXACTLY one, which fails in both directions (0 = the winning conversion never landed, 2 = both tabs converted); (c) the test also asserts tab 1 recorded "created successfully" - without it, a build where BOTH tabs failed would still satisfy "tab 2 showed an error" and pass a race that never had a winner.

column2: Verify that when an RFX Award is performed with long text entered in the Justification fields, hovering over the text displays the complete entered text.
column4: 300-char justification text is entered, awarded, and shown in full on hover (@S21)
column5:
Builds its own data - the recorded blocker was that Justification is empty on every existing award, so the only way to get a truncated value is to award one.
1. CXO -> Intake -> convert to RFX -> quote from CAPP -> FORECLOSE (shared buildRfxToForeclose).
2. Analysis tab -> Award. The form MUST be reached by CLICKING Award: navigating straight to /rfx/<id>/new-award renders an INCOMPLETE form with the "Remarks" and "Attachments" rows absent and every row below shifted up.
3. Fill Remarks and Initial Quote Remarks with EXACTLY 300 characters each, each carrying a terminal marker so truncation is provable. Rows are resolved by LABEL, never by index - the visible "#" column disagrees with the DOM row id and the ids shift between renders.
4. Fill the Allocated Quantity from Pending Awarded Quantity, as the other chains do.
5. Submit the award, confirm its Workflow Summary, clear its approvals (reassigning the approver when the stage is not assigned to this login).
6. On the resulting award page, hover each field and assert: the reveal carries the complete 300 chars, and the cell is genuinely CLIPPED (otherwise the value would be readable without hovering and the check proves nothing). Scrollability is asserted only where the reveal actually overflows.
column6: Long Justification text is stored in full and the complete value is displayed on hover.
column7: PASS - automated and verified 2026-09-07 on RFX 1478 / award 704 (2 passed). Remarks and Initial Quote Remarks each accepted 300 chars; both cells clip the value (scrollWidth 2018 and 1988 vs clientWidth 662) and hovering reveals all 300 characters. MEASURED: the hover tooltip is a 360x141 box reporting scrollHeight 141 == clientHeight 141 - it WRAPS the whole value and needs NO scrolling at 300 chars, so the scroll branch is dormant. Forcing it would need roughly 1500+ chars. CAVEAT: the Remarks tooltip node reports 601 chars for the 300-char value because the container accumulates its child text, so exact-match is proven for Initial Quote Remarks (exact=true) but not for Remarks. FOUND EN ROUTE, SHARED FIX: clickSubmit() waited only 5s for the Workflow Summary confirmation modal, which renders only after the server analyses the approval conditions. The modal was on screen while the caller was already polling for a URL change, so the CXO never submitted and the chain died at step one. Now polls 30s for the dialog OR an early navigation and requires the dialog to close. This affects EVERY chain-based suite, not just 21. CAVEAT: verified in two parts. The full chain run drove CXO -> ... -> award and BOTH hover assertions passed, but the test then died on a summary console.log referencing a field the helper no longer returns; the corrected code plus the tightened reveal-node selection was then verified via S21_AWARD_URL against RFX 1478 / award 704 (2 passed, 24.7s). The complete path has not yet run end to end in one piece.

PASS end to end (live 2026-09-02, 4.1 min): built RFX-26-242 from INT-FNSE-26-374, created the evaluation, answered 4 questions, quoted, foreclosed, rated all 3 answers 5/5 with reasons -> submit returned 200 -> status Completed, 3/3 answers green, Activity Log shows 'Evaluation has been submitted by NSEF Support Admin'.
DEFECT-SHAPED BEHAVIOUR WORTH KNOWING: per-answer ticks save NOTHING to the server - ratings are held in the browser and the header tick posts them all at once. If one star click is swallowed the header tick still submits the rest, and the evaluation lands on 'Partially Completed' with that answer left uncoloured and no warning. column2: Verify that supplier Create and Onboarding is working properly in CAPP Flow
column4: Create Supplier form opens with its sections / a registered supplier exposes its Onboarding tab / a supplier can be created, approved and sent for onboarding / the supplier onboarding form can be completed and submitted
column5:
1. Open /suppliers, switch to the All tab, click Add New and assert the Create Supplier form renders its Supplier Details and User Details sections.
2. Separately, open the first supplier whose Registration Status is Registered, click its Onboarding tab and assert the supplier's details render there.
3. CREATE: fill the mandatory set (Name = "HG Auto Supplier <stamp>", Payment Spoc, Alternate Supplier Name, NDA required?, one User Details row) and Submit via getByRole (the form embeds a SunEditor that injects HIDDEN Submit buttons; an XPath text match hits one of those and the click does nothing).
4. Confirm the Workflow Summary popup - stages: Sup Create Approval, Sup Create Ack, Sup Create Review.
5. Approve every stage until the status reads Submitted (Approve -> Acknowledge -> Review via the edit drawer).
6. Send Onboarding, leaving the pre-selected template unchanged; assert the request is accepted and the status moves to Requested.
7. ONBOARDING FORM (/suppliers/<id>/update): submit once empty, read the "<field> is Mandatory" messages and fill only those, repeating until nothing new appears (the form is progressive - answering GST = No adds "No GST Acknowledgment"). Yes/No questions are answered No per QA.
8. Sweep every attachment wrapper on the form and upload into any that still holds no file, so no mandatory attachment can be missed.
9. Submit; assert nothing skipped, nothing still outstanding, every attachment field holds a file, and the write is accepted.
10. Approve the ONBOARDING workflow (3 further Approve stages) and assert the supplier reaches Pending Sync.
column6: Supplier create and onboarding work in the CAPP flow: the onboarding form submits and its approvals carry the supplier to Pending Sync.
column7: PASS - full flow verified 2026-09-07. Created FNSE-26-3040 (/suppliers/30716), cleared all 3 create stages in exactly 3 actions to Submitted, Send Onboarding with template "Default Supplier Onboarding" -> Requested. Onboarding form: 65 mandatory fields on pass 1, 1 progressive field on pass 2, 0 on pass 3; 29 pickers, 31 text, 2 dates, 4 attachments, 0 skipped, 23 Yes/No answered No, submit HTTP 200. Onboarding approvals then clear 3 Approve stages and land on Pending Sync (re-verified on FNSE-26-3035, 2 passed in 5.0m). DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the filler routed the NDA ATTACHMENT into the date picker, because getByPlaceholder does SUBSTRING matching and "Enter NDA" is a substring of the date input "Enter NDA Start Date". NDA was never uploaded, the submit was refused, and the run reported http=null with NDA only listed as "skipped". Date placeholders are now matched EXACTLY, attachments are checked before dates, and every attachment wrapper is swept before submit. END STATE IS PENDING SYNC, per QA: the Pending Sync -> Registered step is driven by the downstream integration, which does not complete in this UAT (FNSE-26-3040 was still Pending Sync minutes after its approvals cleared). That transition is scenario 141, not 97. NOTE: the form carries 31 attachment fields, of which 4 are mandatory (NDA, Code of Conduct, File Upload with Template, No GST Acknowledgment); the sweep currently fills all 31. NOTE ON TIMEOUTS: no CLI --timeout is needed. test.setTimeout() in the test body DOES override the config's 30s global - verified 2026-09-07 by running test 4 alone with no --timeout: 2 passed in 2.7m. An earlier run reported "Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded" alongside a genuine 15s autocomplete failure; that 30000 figure is the config global being echoed, not the effective budget, and it has not reproduced.

column2: Verify that duplicate Invoice reference numbers are validated when an existing Invoice is edited and submitted.

6. SAPP: create an invoice against that PO - it lands in CAPP as Pending Review.
7. CAPP: More -> Reassign Workflow Approver, match line items to the GRN, then Review -> /invoices/<id>/edit.
8. Set Invoice Number to the collision, submit, and assert the validation is DISPLAYED and names the colliding invoice.

column7: PASS - both halves. CREATION HALF verified 2026-09-07 (2 passed, 48.0s): re-using INV-AUTO-112 gave a hard block - modal "Invoice has failed duplicate validation. Please refer to Invoice-FNSE-26-367" with Proceed DISABLED. REVIEW HALF: setting Invoice Number to INV-AUTO-116 on the review edit page was refused with "Invoice has failed duplicate validation. Please refer to Invoice-FNSE-26-369". ONE FLOW covers both, per QA 2026-09-08 - a Pending-Review invoice costs ~17 min of chain to produce, and both checks live on the same review edit page. Order: over-long Subject -> assert the limit validation -> re-enter review (which restores the Subject) -> duplicate reference -> assert the duplicate validation. ROUTE: creating the invoice from SAPP is what triggers the Review stage; the checks are CAPP-side on /invoices/<id>/edit, reached by More -> Reassign Workflow Approver -> match line items -> Review. A CAPP-created PO invoice goes straight to Pending Approval, so SAPP is the only door. A FRESH PO is required: one that already carries an invoice hits the known "2nd invoice sends the full PO qty" bug, whose silent-stall symptom is indistinguishable from a validation refusal. Verified live 2026-09-08 on Invoice-FNSE-26-376 (/invoices/1151, pending-review), 2 passed in 1.9 min. SIX TRAPS, every one of which produced a WRONG result first: (1) the More button was given 8s and the page renders it late, so the reassign that unlocks Review was skipped; (2) readSavedInvoiceNumber read the body once with no retry; (3) the Item Matching dialog has a shape with neither Add GRN nor Submit, and a hard 10s wait for that Submit took the whole test down; (4) the GRN lookup demanded an exact code with no fallback (savedGrn INW-NSEFN-26-113 vs the PO's actual INW-NSEFN-26-114); (5) appending //button to the muiDialog locator was an XPath PRECEDENCE BUG - that locator is a union (A | B), so the suffix binds to B alone and .first() matched the dialog DIV, meaning the Proceed click landed on the dialog body and was silently swallowed; (6) the subject validation is TRANSIENT - the Workflow Summary dialog does NOT change when it fires, so a click-then-verify-the-dialog-changed helper concluded the click was swallowed, clicked three more times, and by the time it scanned the message had auto-dismissed. The DEFAULT path, which builds its own chain CXO -> ... -> PO -> GRN, has not been re-run end to end since these fixes - though its chain build did complete cleanly in 17.6 min on 2026-09-08 and produced the very invoice these assertions passed against.

column2: Verify that rejecting or sending back an Invoice at the Review stage updates its status correctly across all applicable pages and reports.
column4: a rejected CXO / PO / Invoice is not in its pending-approval view (3 tests)
column5:
For each of CXO, PO and Invoice:
1. Build the transaction and leave it in Pending Approval (the PO chain runs with { approvePo: false }).
2. Reject it - rejectCxo for the CXO, rejectCappDoc for the PO and Invoice.
3. Open that module's listing and switch to its pending-approval view (label differs per module - see the note).

column6: A rejected transaction no longer appears in the pending-approval view of its listing.
column7: PASS - verified live 2026-09-08 (CXO: 2 passed in 1.6 min; PO + Invoice: 3 passed in 31.1 min). CXO-FNSE-26-403, PO-NSEFN-26-228 and Invoice-FNSE-26-384 were each built, left in Pending Approval, rejected, and then confirmed ABSENT from their module's pending-approval view. QA reframed the sheet's vague "across all applicable pages and reports" into a concrete check on 2026-09-08: after rejecting, the listing's pending-approval view must not show the transaction. SCOPE - CXO, PO and Invoice ONLY, on QA's instruction. The other modules were probed live and have no such view: GRN's /inwards listing shows no approval text at all, and Intake and RFX offer only "All". NOTE an Intake tab_MyPendingApproval locator DOES exist in the repo and is mapped in intakeListingActions, but no test ever exercised it and the live listing does not render it - so its presence was never real. TRAP: THE LABEL DIFFERS BY MODULE. CXO and Invoice use "My Pending Approval"; the PO listing uses "Pending My Approval" - different WORD ORDER. Matching one string everywhere finds nothing on the PO listing and would pass for the wrong reason. CXO is a v4 role=tab; PO and Invoice are v3 plain-text controls. SCAN DEPTH, stated rather than assumed: the CXO view PAGINATES and 47 codes were walked. The PO and Invoice views return ONE page of 20 rows - and that is not a helper limitation: probed live, they expose no pagination control at all (no Next, no pager icons, no "Showing X of Z" footer), so there is no page 2 to miss, but the queue's true size cannot be read either. The assertion leans on newest-first ordering putting a just-rejected record on page 1. The Invoice case matches its GRN deliberately - an UNMATCHED invoice goes to Disputed (scenario 69) and so would never enter the approval queue. The Invoice reject also needed the workflow approver reassigned to NSEF Support Admin before Reject rendered, which rejectCappDoc handles.
